gaps.description: The doc has no default or optional parameters, so every caller must pass both functions.

gaps.construct: defaults reach time.monotonic and time.sleep with no capability passed in
gaps.description: A default that reads the clock or sleeps would need a capability the caller never handed over. Example 22 says authority enters only at main, so such a default cannot be expressed even if defaults existed.

gaps.construct: self.timefunc / self.delayfunc stored in the instance
gaps.description: There is no type for an operation held in a field or variable; `an Operation producing a Number` is invented.
The doc removes locks by design (example 38) and has no lock type, so the lock that guards the queue across threads cannot be expressed.
There are no generators or iterators that hold state. A Nat counter field stands in for it, and every use must read it and then increase it by hand.
There are no classes or constructors. The constructor becomes an operation that produces a new record, which works but changes the API shape.

gaps.construct: building a record value field by field
gaps.description: The only record construction shown is `an Order from cart and receipt with status Paid`. The doc gives no general field-by-field literal.
Example 21 says allocation must use an Allocator, but the doc does not say how a list literal or a library object names its allocator.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one. (The original's lock exists so other threads can share the scheduler's queue.)
invented_syntax: an Operation producing a Number / an Operation taking a Number (function types)
a Scheduler with queue [] and lock new_lock and timefunc timefunc and ... (record literal with one with-clause per field)
notes: The constructor itself is trivial; every gap comes from what the object is designed to do: hold injectable callbacks, be shared between threads under a lock, and default to ambient clock authority. Scribe's capability model would replace 'timefunc defaults to the wall clock' with 'pass a Clock', which is arguably better, but the injected-function design (used for testing with fake clocks) has no equivalent until function values exist.
